title: Exported node references to instanced scene are silently removed when nodes are renamed
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.8.dev [8dbf8a899], 4.6.3.stable

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (8dbf8a899) - Fedora Linux 44 (Forty Four) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When renaming a node in a scene, where that scene is instanced in another "outer" scene, and the outer scene has a saved/serialized `@export` reference to a node in the first/inner scene, you will find that the saved/serialized reference is silently removed when saving the outer scene again.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP.
2. Open `outer.tscn` in a text editor.
3. Note how `outer.tscn` has a `inner_child = NodePath("Inner/InnerChild")`.
4. Open `inner.tscn` in Godot.
5. Rename `InnerChild` to `RenamedChild`.
6. Open `outer.tscn` in Godot.
7. Save `outer.tscn`.
8. Open `outer.tscn` in a text editor.
9. Note how the `inner_child = NodePath("Inner/InnerChild")` is now gone.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[dropped-node-paths.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29551576/dropped-node-paths.zip)
